props.title: Play It Again, Sam
props.initialSlug: Neurotic writer seeks love with Bogart's ghostly help

sections.content: Play It Again, Sam (1972) brilliantly merges Woody Allen's neurotic comedy with his love of classic cinema, particularly Casablanca (1942). Allen plays Allan Felix, a recently divorced film critic obsessed with Humphrey Bogart, who appears as his imaginary mentor. The film explores romance through a cinephile's lens, mixing reality with movie fantasy as Allan navigates dating in San Francisco with advice from his idealized Bogart.

sections.content: The film establishes themes that would define Allen's later work - the intersection of art and life, romantic idealization, and self-deprecating humor. Like Manhattan (1979) and Annie Hall (1977), it uses cultural touchstones to examine modern relationships. The protagonist's Bogart fixation mirrors how we often measure our lives against movie ideals. SUBHEAD: Cinema as Life Reference Point

Director Herbert Ross captures Allen's script with a perfect balance of homage and originality. While clearly referencing Casablanca (1942), the film creates its own identity through clever parallel scenes and dialogue that comment on how movies shape our romantic expectations. This meta-commentary influenced later films like The Purple Rose of Cairo (1985) and Cinema Paradiso (1988).
